answer: A pearl farm maps its reef as a grid, and each agent holds one vertex where a single oyster bed grows. To keep the vertex, the agent dives at low tide, opens one oyster, and lifts a pearl still seated in its shell, then locks it into a ferrous tag stamped with the vertex number. A second diver checks the tag a week later and cuts any vertex whose pearl is missing or swapped. A thousand fake names need a thousand dives, a thousand pearls, and a thousand stamped tags, and no copied ledger can fake one tide of cold water work.
